title: Deep muscles of the anterior and medial thigh (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Greater trochanter and the lateral lip of the linea aspera of the femur.
Patella through the quadriceps tendon, and through the patellar ligament the tibial tuberosity.
Extends the leg at the knee.
Anterior and lateral surfaces of the shaft of the femur.
Patella through the quadriceps tendon, and through the patellar ligament the tibial tuberosity.
Extends the leg at the knee.
Intertrochanteric line and the medial lip of the linea aspera of the femur.
Patella through the quadriceps tendon, and through the patellar ligament the tibial tuberosity.
Extends the leg at the knee. Its lowest fibers pull the patella medially and keep it in its groove.
Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
Pectineal line and the upper part of the linea aspera of the femur.
Adductor part from the inferior ramus of the pubis and the ramus of the ischium. Hamstring part from the ischial tuberosity.
Adductor part on the linea aspera and the medial supracondylar line of the femur. Hamstring part on the adductor tubercle.
Adductor part by the obturator nerve (L2 to L4). Hamstring part by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L4).
Adducts the thigh. The adductor part also flexes the thigh and the hamstring part extends it.
hy: The gap between its two insertions is the adductor hiatus. The femoral artery and vein pass through it to the back of the knee, where they become the popliteal artery and vein.

rows: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
Upper part of the medial surface of the tibia, with sartorius and semitendinosus (pes anserinus).
Adducts the thigh, flexes the leg at the knee and helps rotate the flexed leg medially.
Outer surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around the obturator foramen.
